question: According to Section 9.4, what types of transactions are allowed for a Wholly‑Owned Subsidiary of the Borrower without violating the Fundamental Changes restriction?

evidence.span_text: (a) (i) any Wholly‑Owned Subsidiary of the Borrower may be merged, amalgamated or consolidated with or into the Borrower (provided that the Borrower shall be the continuing or surviving entity) or (ii) any Wholly‑Owned Subsidiary of the Borrower may be merged, amalgamated or consolidated with or into any Subsidiary Guarantor (provided that the Subsidiary Guarantor shall be the continuing or surviving entity or simultaneously with such transaction, the continuing or surviving entity shall become a Subsidiary Guarantor and the Borrower shall comply with Section 8.14 in connection therewith).

reference_answer: A Wholly‑Owned Subsidiary may be merged, amalgamated or consolidated with the Borrower, provided the Borrower is the surviving entity, or it may be merged, amalgamated or consolidated with a Subsidiary Guarantor, provided the Subsidiary Guarantor survives and the Borrower complies with Section 8.14. These are the only permitted combinations for a Wholly‑Owned Subsidiary under the Fundamental Changes clause.
key_points: Borrower must be surviving entity in first case
Subsidiary Guarantor must survive and Borrower must comply with Section 8.14 in second case

question: What events trigger a "Change in Law" under this Agreement, and are there any specific statutes or regulatory frameworks that are automatically considered a Change in Law regardless of when they are enacted?

evidence.span_text: "Change in Law" means the occurrence after the date of this Agreement of any of the following: (a) the adoption of or taking effect of any law, rule, regulation or treaty, (b) any change in any law, rule, regulation or treaty or in the administration, interpretation, implementation or application thereof by any Governmental Authority or (c) compliance by the Lender ... with any request, guideline, requirement or directive (whether or not having the force of law) of any Governmental Authority made or issued after the date of this Agreement; provided that, notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, (x) the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act ... and (y) all requests, rules, guidelines, requirements or directives promulgated by the Bank for International Settlements, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision ... pursuant to Basel III, shall in each case be deemed to be a "Change in Law"

reference_answer: A Change in Law is triggered by (a) the adoption or effective date of any new law, rule, regulation or treaty, (b) any amendment, reinterpretation or change in administration of existing law or regulation by a governmental authority, or (c) the Lender’s compliance with any post‑agreement request, guideline, requirement or directive from a governmental authority.  Regardless of timing, the Dodd‑Frank Act and any Basel III‑related rules issued by the BIS, the Basel Committee, or U.S. or foreign regulators are deemed a Change in Law.
key_points: adoption or effect of new law/rule/treaty
change or reinterpretation of existing law by authority
Lender compliance with post‑agreement governmental request
Dodd‑Frank and Basel III rules are automatically included

any change in any law, rule, regulation or treaty
